article_notes: Descriptive case series of 49 dogs with autochthonous B. canis (PCR and sequencing) in Berlin/Brandenburg; 46 seen at the university small animal clinic, 3 in a private practice; full data for the 46 clinic dogs. Descriptive statistics only; no statistical test against outcome. Outcome: 39 survived, 4 euthanised (some partly for financial reasons) and 3 died within 2-18 days. The only results set against outcome are SIRS at presentation and persistent azotaemia, given as counts. Laboratory values in Table 1 are for the whole group only. Initial samples at presentation; timing relative to imidocarb not stated.

severity_definitions.label: died or euthanised vs survived
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs that died (n=3) or were euthanised (n=4) during follow-up vs dogs that survived (n=39). Euthanasia reasons included financial reasons combined with acute renal failure.
severity_definitions.quote: Thirty‐nine dogs (85%) survived. Four dogs were euthanized after 2 to 18 days

associations.statistic: SIRS in 3 of 7 dogs that died or were euthanised; 13 dogs with SIRS survived (SIRS in 16 of 43 assessed dogs)
associations.quote: Systemic inflammatory response syndrome occurred in 3 of 7 of the dogs that died or were euthanized in our study, whereas 13 dogs with SIRS survived B. canis infection.
associations.location: Discussion (restates the study's own results; Results: Treatment and outcome)
associations.note: SIRS was assessed in 43 dogs; the number of survivors assessed is not printed, so no comparison-group denominator.

associations.marker_as_reported: persistently increased serum creatinine concentration (renal azotaemia)
associations.statistic: 5 of 17 dogs with persistently increased creatinine died or were euthanised
associations.quote: Five of 17 dogs with persistently increased serum creatinine concentrations died or were euthanized, respectively.
associations.note: Mortality among azotaemic dogs only; mortality in non-azotaemic dogs is not printed. Several deaths were attributed to acute renal failure.
